newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain cuts key rate 25 bps to 6.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain cuts key rate 25 bps to 6.00 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Spain seized one of its first opportunities of the year and sanctioned a cut of one-quarter point to six percent in its key money market rate on Thursday.
The move caught the market by surprise. Only a handful of analysts and dealers had expected a reduction despite the peseta's recent strength and good December inflation data released on Wednesday.
According to a Reuter survey of 10 economists conducted on Wednesday following benign inflation data, only two of those surveyed said they expected a reduction today.

Those who expected a cut pointed to the consumer price data. Inflation in December was just 3.2 percent, the lowest level in nearly 30 years and well beneath the government's 3.4 percent mid-year target.

The peseta's strength had prompted some to consider a reduction. The peseta, encouraged by the dollar's strength against the mark, has barrelled to highs against the German currency that have not been seen since last May.
